description: Issue a refund for an order. This is a WRITE above the approval line, and it works in two steps. FIRST call it with preview set to true: it returns exactly what would happen (order, item, amount) and changes NOTHING. THEN, if the refund is right, call it with preview set to false: that does NOT issue the refund - it submits it to the approval gate as a pending action, and a human must approve it before any money moves. Never tell the customer a refund has been issued; only the approval receipt proves that. If the order was already refunded, this returns an error naming the existing refund.

errors.returns: An error saying order_id is required and what it looks like.
A format error echoing what was sent, naming the ticket-number confusion when the id starts with TKT.
errors.when: order_id is not shaped like ORD-1234

errors.returns: A not-found error suggesting a wrong digit.
errors.when: order_id is well-formed but no such order exists

errors.returns: An error saying a reason is required.
An error naming the existing refund id - refunds are issued once per order.
errors.when: the order already has a refund

order_id.description: The order to refund, e.g. ORD-2077. This is the order id from the customer's confirmation email - NOT the ticket number (which looks like TKT-1042).

preview.description: true = show exactly what would happen and change nothing. false = submit the refund to the approval gate as a pending action (still not issued - a human approves it first). Always preview before submitting.

reason.description: Why the refund is being issued, in a few words from the ticket, e.g. 'item arrived damaged' or 'package lost in transit'.

name: issue_refund
